To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a 2-h ischaemia causes irreversible damage to liver lysosomes, and that the administration of chlorpromazine before or after ischaemia prevents this damage.
a 2-h ischaemia induces an alteration of liver lysosomes that, in the absence of chlorpromazine, is largely reversible and in the presence of this drug is largely irreversible.

(1) the structure-linked latency for rat liver acid phosphatas and beta-galacosidase is decreased by a 2 h transitory ischaemic shock; (2) this latency decrease is prevented by chlorpromazine; (3) the latency decrease is largely reversible after a 1 h ischaemia; (4) after 2 h of ischaemia the latency decrease is only partially reversible.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
a 2-h ischaemia is not sufficient to produce an irreversible lesion, but the restoration of blood flow does.
chlorpromazine treatment protects lysosomes from the irreversible lesion caused by the reoxygenation of ischaemic liver.

the latency changes observed in the present work reflect alterations of the lysosomal membranes, which are reversible when the liver is made ischaemic only for 1 h and irreversible when it is made ischaemia for 2 h.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
chlorpromazine treatment of the liver prevents the lysosomal damage caused by the ischaemic insult.
the lysosomal enzyme structure-linked latency is an important indicator of the integrity of the lysosomal membrane.
chlorpromazine, by preventing the secondary increase of the unmasked hydrolase activity, protects against the irreversible damage of the lysosomes induced by a 2 h of ischaemia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the structure-linked latency is a useful tool to detect and study the effects of an ischaemic injury on the lysosomes of rat liver.
a 2-h period of ischaemic stress induces a reversible alteration of liver lysosomes that can be prevented by chlorpromazine.
the liver is a very complex organ and that there are multiple mechanisms involved in the regulation of the liver’s response to injury.
